title: The Mormons and the Theatre; or, The History of Theatricals in Utah

It delves into how figures like Brigham Young facilitated and promoted theatrical entertainment among Mormons, presenting a narrative of religious life intertwined with the performing arts. The beginning of the book establishes the groundwork for an exploration of Mormon theatre, opening with a description of their enthusiasm for dancing and plays, which contrasts sharply with the practices of many other Christian denominations. Lyne, an actor who became converted to Mormonism and played a significant role in early theatrical productions.
